measured_metrics: Observation: latency_ms per timed repeat, wall-clock via time.perf_counter_ns with torch.cuda.synchronize before and after (resnet_inference.py:42-48)
Observation: images_per_second = workload batch size / elapsed time per repeat
Observation: peak_allocated_bytes from torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated after reset_peak_memory_stats each repeat
Observation: summarize() reports median/min/max per metric across repeats (>=3 enforced by arguments())

Observation: exact top-1 agreement via torch.equal on argmax of both runs; first 3 predicted label strings recorded (resnet_inference.py:33-35)
Observation: reference pixels+logits saved as <workload>-reference.pt per workload for offline inspection
Observation: metadata explicitly scopes quality to 'Reference fidelity; no downstream accuracy/convergence claim' — no ground-truth label validation exists
Observation: determinism-oriented config (TF32 off, matmul precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark off, fixed seed) so checks validate like-for-like runs, not accuracy

Hypothesis: channels_last memory format for the ResNet conv stack on tensor-core GPUs
Hypothesis: larger batch sizes in workloads.json to raise GPU utilization; current batches tile a small fixture set via arange % len(images)
Hypothesis: export path (TorchScript/ONNX/TensorRT) for deployment-grade latency; single-stream python eager loop measured here
Observation constraining the above: baseline is deliberately unoptimized (protocol tag readiness_baseline_not_optimization) and any optimization run must re-pass the close_check/negative_check gates
